policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: Word order only: 'on the third day' renders either the base or the RP transposition identically. Nothing in the ASV or its notes distinguishes them; base fallback carries the projection.
Alternate contracted form of the same comparative; 'the greater part' renders either. No ASV note bears on it.
RP adds an adverbial kai that the ASV need not render; 'but some are fallen asleep' is compatible with either reading, and no note is mapped here.
Presence or absence of the article before charis is invisible in English; the only note here is an alternative_rendering ('Or, void') about the wording of kene.
Word order only: 'some among you' renders either arrangement. No note bears on it.
An added kai after ara that the ASV need not render; 'then is our preaching vain' does not distinguish. The verse's textual_variant note concerns hymon/hemon, not this unit.
RP's connective de is of the sort the ASV commonly leaves unrendered; the asyndetic 'your faith also is vain' does not settle it. The verse's textual_variant note concerns hymon/hemon.

The ASV text reads 'your faith', rendering hymon, and its note 'Some ancient authorities read our' places hemon in the margin — the English text selects the base reading and the note names the rejected one.
Addition of the copula estin is invisible: 'your faith is vain' supplies the verb either way.
Word order only; the sole note is an alternative_rendering about where 'only' attaches in English, which cannot decide a reading.

RP's added egeneto would give 'became the firstfruits of them that are asleep'. The ASV renders a bare appositive — 'the firstfruits of them that are asleep' — with no second finite verb, so the base reading without egeneto is what stands behind the English.
Presence of the article with thanatos is invisible in 'by man came death'.
Present and aorist subjunctive forms of paradidomi are all rendered by 'when he shall deliver up'; the only note is a greek_gloss on 'the God and Father'.
The particle an with achri hou is untranslatable separately; 'till he hath put' renders either.

The ASV reads 'then shall the Son also himself be subjected'. 'Himself' already renders autos, so the additional 'also' renders the kai of the longer reading; the base without kai would give only 'then shall the Son himself'.
Article with panta is invisible in 'that God may be all in all'.
The ASV closes the verse with the pronoun 'why then are they baptized for them?', rendering hyper auton; RP's ton nekron would have repeated 'for the dead' as at the verse's opening.
The ASV has the vocative 'brethren' in 'by that glorying in you, brethren, which I have in Christ Jesus our Lord' — adelphoi is rendered, so the longer reading stands behind the English.
lalo and lego are both rendered 'I speak'; nothing in the ASV distinguishes them.
Nominative-for-vocative aphron and the vocative Aphron are both rendered 'Thou foolish one'.
Word order only: 'God giveth it a body' renders either arrangement.
Article with idion is invisible in 'a body of its own'.
The ASV lists 'another flesh of birds, and another of fishes' — birds in the third slot and fishes in the fourth, which is the base order; RP's transposition puts fishes third.
The fourth member in the ASV is 'another of fishes', matching the base ichthyon at this position; RP reads birds here.
The ASV renders the conditional protasis explicitly — 'If there is a natural body, there is also a spiritual body' — so ei is present, against RP's omission.

The apodosis in the ASV is 'there is also a spiritual body', with the adverbial 'also' following the verb as estin kai does; RP's kai estin soma would give a coordinating 'and there is a spiritual body', which the ASV does not have.
The ASV reads simply 'the second man is of heaven', with no rendering of RP's added ho kyrios ('the Lord from heaven').

The ASV text has the future indicative 'we shall also bear the image of the heavenly' (phoresomen), and its note 'Many ancient authorities read let us also bear' assigns the hortatory subjunctive phoresomen/phoreswmen to the margin.
Singular or plural verb with 'flesh and blood' is invisible in English 'cannot inherit'.
RP's men is a correlative particle the ASV need not render; the note here is an alternative_rendering about the placement of 'all' with the negative, which cannot decide a reading.

The ASV text prints the longer clause 'But when this corruptible shall have put on incorruption, and this mortal...', and its note 'Many ancient authorities omit this corruptible shall have put on incorruption, and' explicitly assigns the omission to the margin.
Article with athanasian is invisible in 'shall have put on immortality'; the verse's textual_variant note concerns the omitted clause, not this unit.

The ASV has 'victory' first and 'sting' second and addresses death both times, which excludes RP's order with Hades ('sting... O Hades, thy victory'). The base and r01 differ only in printed punctuation, which the English cannot distinguish.
